title: Silhouette
description: A silhouette shot places the subject dark against a brighter background so the figure reads as shape, not as a modeled face. Gesture and contour do the work; surface detail is gone.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Identity is less important than emblem: a rider on a ridge, a bicycle against a moon, a man in a doorway. The audience recognizes an action from outline alone.
If two shapes merge, the sentence is lost. It is the wrong tool when a line of dialogue needs a mouth, or when you still want pores and color in the coat.
A little rim is not a silhouette. If you can name the eye color, you overexposed the figure.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Expose for the bright ground (sky, doorway, fire, sun disk). Keep the key off the subject, or far below the background.
Backlight may exist as a sky, not as a facial key. Separate limbs, hats, and props so the outline parses.

Hardness of the background source can be hard sun or a bright overcast; the subject is simply underexposed. Prompt: Silhouette of [Subject] as a dark shape against a bright ground, surface detail gone, mythic outline only.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when identity matters less than shape, a departure through a door, a figure against dusk. Do not use it if the action cannot be read from the outline.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Backlight can create a silhouette if you expose for it, or a rim if you hold the face a little. Rim light keeps a thread of flesh highlight; silhouette usually does not.
Cameo lighting is the inverse: a lit figure on a black ground. Low-key lighting still models something in the pool.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: T. the Extra-Terrestrial puts bicycle and riders in silhouette across the moon.
The Searchers isolates a figure against a bright doorway and landscape. Lawrence of Arabia and Skyfall use desert and sun as the bright field that turns bodies into emblems.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Expose the ground, starve the body. " Name a readable outline (limbs separated).
Forbid facial detail and neon rims.

A parent and child carry a small telescope up a ridge at dusk, rendered as clean dark silhouettes against a luminous pale sky. Keep their limbs and the telescope distinct. Locked wide view, gentle wind, no visible facial detail or artificial rim halo.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a rim portrait or a muddy underexposure on a dark ground. The tell is visible eyes, or a black figure on a black field.
Fix it by brightening the background, killing keys on the body, and separating the limbs.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is a silhouette in film?
A subject placed dark against a brighter background so contour and gesture read instead of facial detail.
Silhouette vs rim light
A silhouette is an unmodeled dark shape on a bright field. Rim light keeps a thin highlight on the edge of a still-dark figure, often on a dark field.
When should I use a silhouette?
Use it when the outline is the sentence: departure, arrival, emblem. Skip it when the face must speak.
How do I prompt a silhouette for AI image or video?
Ask for a dark shape against a bright ground, no surface detail, limbs separated. Expose for the sky or doorway, not the face.
